title: Correctness: FIPS gate called AFTER copy_from_user in ioctl_set_iv/gen_iv/set_aad/get_tag/set_tag, not as first statement
description:
Trigger: call CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_SET_IV (or SET_AAD, GET_TAG, SET_TAG, GEN_IV) on an OPERATION fd after the FIPS provider enters a degraded state.

In ioctl_set_iv (and all other per-operation ioctls except INIT), the sequence is:
  1. copy_from_user(&op, ...) — reads user data into kernel op struct
  2. validate op fields (ivlen bounds check, etc.)
  3. mutex_lock(&state->lock)
  4. if (state->ops && state->ops->fips_gate) { ... }

The FIPS gate is the FOURTH step, not the first. Steps 1-2 happen before the FIPS gate is checked.

FIPS 140-3 operational requirement and the project's own critical design rule (CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md): the FIPS gate must be the very first line of every crypto entry point, before argument validation, before lock acquisition, before anything else.

For SET_IV specifically: the user buffer is read (step 1) and validated (step 2) before the gate fires. A FIPS violation can be detected only after consuming user data.

Contrast with ioctl_init, which checks the gate after copy_from_user and validation — this has the same problem.

The correct pattern per the paranoid checklist is: fips_gate() → if (ret) return ret — as the FIRST executable statement, with no preceding copy_from_user or field checks.

The practical consequence is minor (reading a valid user buffer is not a security boundary breach), but it is a documented violation of the FIPS 140-3 operational requirement as stated in the project's own design rules and the CMVP submission.
